answer: An agent economy resists sybils by paying rewards only from real service fees: an identity earns a share of fees paid by established users for work it actually delivered, like a bridge toll collected only from travellers who crossed. A fake's copper coins come only from genuine customers, and the pigment of its ledger stays blank without them. Self-payments fail because the payer must itself be established, so a farm funding its own fakes spends as much as it earns — cloning multiplies cost, never profit.
